walkthroughs.body_html:
Food, Nutrition and Health — a core area of GCSE Food Preparation and Nutrition.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Food, Nutrition and Health brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Food, Nutrition and Health.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What are the 4 Cs of food hygiene?
options: Chopping, Cleaning, Cooling, Carrying.
Pickling adds extra nutrients.
Calories, Carbs, Calcium, Cholesterol.
Cleaning, Cooking, Chilling, and avoiding Cross-contamination.

mcqs.q: On a traffic-light label, what does a red light indicate?
options: High amounts of that nutrient per 100g - eat less often.
The food is organic.
The food is dangerous and should never be eaten.
Calories, Carbs, Calcium, Cholesterol.
Acidic conditions (low pH) prevent most bacteria from growing.
The food is organic.
The vinegar kills the food cells.
Pickling adds extra nutrients.
